title: 🚨 A massive financial crisis could be brewing for Anthropic. Just days after its record breaking IPO, Wall Street is expecting Anthropic's bonds to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ. And this comes as its stock has already crashed below its $83 IPO
title_en:
🚨 A massive financial crisis could be brewing for Anthropic.

Just days after its record breaking IPO, Wall Street is expecting Anthropic's bonds to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ.

And this comes as its stock has already crashed below its $83 IPO price.

But the bigger problem is Anthropic's MASSIVE AI spending commitments.

Here's what's happening:

• Anthropic has committed to spending $900 BILLION on AI computing power over the coming years.

• The company generated $17 BILLION in revenue last quarter, yet it's still losing money due to its enormous computing costs.

• Anthropic has $96 BILLION in cash, but its future spending commitments are nearly 10 times that amount.

• Bond investors expect its debt to receive a BB rating, below investment grade, which could make borrowing significantly more expensive.

• The entire U.S. junk bond market is worth just $1.7 TRILLION, making it difficult to raise hundreds of billions through traditional high-yield bonds.

And the implications go far beyond Anthropic.

NVIDIA and Broadcom have already guaranteed tens of billions in loans tied to AI chip purchases, while lenders are becoming increasingly concerned about the industry's massive borrowing needs.

Even established tech giants are struggling to attract bond investors, with some AI-related bonds already suffering significant losses.

Anthropic has raised enormous amounts of cash, but roughly HALF of its spending commitments stretch from 2031 all the way to 2045.

That means the company will need access to affordable financing for YEARS.

If its debt receives a junk rating, borrowing could become much more expensive, putting pressure on its AI expansion plans.

And if a company worth over $1 TRILLION struggles to finance its AI spending, the damage could spread to chipmakers, data centers and the entire AI industry.

title: Benchmark grading is getting honest. Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 asks one question only: would a real open source maintainer actually merge this pull request. Every model that took the test scored lower than it did on the easier 1.1 version, including Cogniti
title_en:
Benchmark grading is getting honest. Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 asks one question only: would a real open source maintainer actually merge this pull request. Every model that took the test scored lower than it did on the easier 1.1 version, including Cognition's own.

SWE-2.1 lands at 41.3 on that harder scale, up from 24.1 for the previous version, and it was built by running reinforcement learning on top of Moonshot's Kimi K3 rather than pretraining a new base model from scratch. That beats Kimi K3.1 itself, the newer tuned version of its own base, which only scores 19.9. Claude Opus 5.5 still tops the board at 45.5%, but that is down from 54.6% on FrontierCode 1.1, so the harder grading hit the leader hardest.

Cost is where it gets interesting. GPT-6.1 Sol scores 39.0% at $1.03 per task. Opus 5.5 costs $12.82 per task for six and a half more points. Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores lower than Opus at 41.0% while costing more per task, $19.94. GPT-6 Astra sits at 42.8% for $6.68. The pattern holding across the leaderboard is that higher reasoning effort does not reliably buy a higher score, and sometimes buys a lower one. Price and capability have quietly come apart.

What FrontierCode actually measures is whether a human maintainer would trust the code enough to ship it, graded on mergeability rather than whether a test suite passes. Tasks this round came from 55% more repositories than 1.1 and touched far more files per fix. That is a meaningfully different bar than SWE-bench ever set, and it is why a model fine-tuned on a Chinese open-weight base can close most of the gap to a frontier proprietary model for a fraction of the training cost, while still falling short of it on the one metric that was supposed to be hardest to game.

My read: the benchmarks are finally catching up to how skeptical working engineers already were about agent-written code, and a 41% to 45% top score on mergeability proves the point better than any vendor demo could. This category still has a long way to go before it can grade itself honestly.

summary_zh:
WE-2.1 在这个难度等级上的得分为 41.3，高于之前版本的 24.1，并且它是通过在 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 上运行强化学习而构建的，而不是从头开始预训练新的基础模型。这击败了 Kimi K3.1 本身，它是自己底座的更新版本，得分仅为 19.9。 Claude Opus 5.5 仍然以 45.5% 的成绩位居榜首，但这低于 FrontierCode 1.1 上的 54.6%，因此更难的评分对领先者的打击最大。

成本是它变得有趣的地方。 GPT-6.1 Sol 在每项任务 1.03 美元的情况下得分为 39.0%。 Opus 5.5 每项任务的成本为 12.82 美元，多了六个半点。 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的得分低于 Opus，为 41.0%，但每项任务的成本更高，为 19.94 美元。 GPT-6 Astra 的售价为 42.8%，价格为 6.68 美元。排行榜上的普遍规律是，较高的推理努力并不能可靠地换来较高的分数，有时甚至会换来较低的分数。价格和功能已经悄然分离。

FrontierCode 实际上衡量的是人类维护人员是否足够信任代码来交付它，根据可合并性而不是测试套件是否通过进行评分。这一轮的任务来自比 1.1 多 55% 的存储库，并且每个修复涉及更多的文件。这与 SWE-bench 所设定的标准有很大不同，这就是为什么在中国开放重量基础上进行微调的模型可以以一小部分训练成本缩小与前沿专有模型的大部分差距，同时在一个被认为是最难竞争的指标上仍然达不到它。

我的解读是：基准测试终于赶上了工作工程师对代理编写的代码的怀疑程度，并且可合并性上 41% 到 45% 的最高分比任何供应商演示都更好地证明了这一点。这个类别距离诚实地给自己评分还有很长的路要走。

That is a meaningfully different bar than SWE-bench ever set, and it is why a model fine-tuned on a Chinese open-weight base can close most of the gap to a frontier proprietary model for a fraction of the training cost, while still falling short of it on the one metric that was supposed to be hardest to game.

My read: the benchmarks are finally catching up to how skeptical working engineers already were about agent-written code, and a 41% to 45% top score on mergeability proves the point better than any vendor demo could. This category still has a long way to go before it can grade itself honestly.

https://x.com/cognition/status/2125305349414523061
full_text_zh:
基准评分变得越来越诚实。 Cognition 的 FrontierCode 2.0 仅提出一个问题：真正的开源维护者是否会真正合并此拉取请求。每个参加测试的模型的得分都低于更简单的 1.1 版本，包括 Cognition 自己的模型。

SWE-2.1 在这个难度等级上的得分为 41.3，高于之前版本的 24.1，并且它是通过在 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 上运行强化学习而构建的，而不是从头开始预训练新的基础模型。这击败了 Kimi K3.1 本身，它是自己底座的更新版本，得分仅为 19.9。 Claude Opus 5.5 仍然以 45.5% 的成绩位居榜首，但这低于 FrontierCode 1.1 上的 54.6%，因此更难的评分对领先者的打击最大。

成本是它变得有趣的地方。 GPT-6.1 Sol 在每项任务 1.03 美元的情况下得分为 39.0%。 Opus 5.5 每项任务的成本为 12.82 美元，多了六个半点。 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的得分低于 Opus，为 41.0%，但每项任务的成本更高，为 19.94 美元。 GPT-6 Astra 的售价为 42.8%，价格为 6.68 美元。排行榜上的普遍规律是，较高的推理努力并不能可靠地换来较高的分数，有时甚至会换来较低的分数。价格和功能已经悄然分离。

FrontierCode 实际上衡量的是人类维护人员是否足够信任代码来交付它，根据可合并性而不是测试套件是否通过进行评分。这一轮的任务来自比 1.1 多 55% 的存储库，并且每个修复涉及更多的文件。这与 SWE-bench 所设定的标准有很大不同，这就是为什么在中国开放重量基础上进行微调的模型可以以一小部分训练成本缩小与前沿专有模型的大部分差距，同时在一个被认为是最难竞争的指标上仍然达不到它。

我的解读是：基准测试终于赶上了工作工程师对代理编写的代码的怀疑程度，并且可合并性上 41% 到 45% 的最高分比任何供应商演示都更好地证明了这一点。这个类别距离诚实地给自己评分还有很长的路要走。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic在模型上下文协议（MCP）两周年之际，推出了Skills over MCP公测版。该功能允许服务器发布包含工作流与操作手册的‘技能’，而非仅限于工具调用，并全面开放了处理长时任务的Tasks和支持用户决策确认的Elicitation功能。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Marking the second anniversary of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Anthropic has launched the public beta of 'Skills over MCP.' This enables servers to provide structured workflows rather than just tool definitions, while also launching general availability for 'Tasks' and 'Elicitation' to handle long-running, interactive agentic workflows.

elements_zh.why: 解决大模型在复杂、多步骤、长时交互任务中上下文管理及任务执行的断点问题

elements_en.what: Released Skills over MCP (beta), Tasks/Elicitation (GA), and upcoming File Uploads
elements_en.why: Addressing context management and task execution continuity challenges in long-running, multi-step agentic workflows.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Anthropic is building a closed-loop agent collaboration standard via the MCP, evolving from simple tool calls to automation based on structured 'Expert Knowledge Flows (Skills).' This strategy aims to unify the fragmented plugin landscape and establish MCP as the foundational infrastructure for enterprise AI agent ecosystems.

title_en: I think this underestimates how much lawyers enjoy some of this “grunt”work that AI is supposed to automate away.  I hear this constantly from lawyers and teams I speak with. Also, when your entire day becomes high judgment/thinking it’s very draining. There is something in the balance of having some technical work and some high judgment work in your day. Review only is very exhausting.

A solo developer just vibe-coded his first game and made $1.33 million on Steam in just one week.

His game, Slotbound, has sold over 200,000 copies in six days and has a 91% Very Positive rating.

title: OpenAI publishes a preprint claiming to prove that the matrix multiplication exponent (ω) is exactly 9/4, addressing a major open problem in mathematics (Deedy/@deedydas)
title_en:
OpenAI just dropped a 111-page proof of a 57-year old math problem: the matrix multiplication exponent (ω) is exactly 9/4.

This problem ranks #31 on ProofAtlas’ top 500 open problems in math and is arguably 2nd only to P = NP in algorithms. 

The problem:
How many steps does it take to multiply two n×n matrices? The schoolbook method takes n^3. The true cost is n^ω. What is ω?

The history:
- 1969: Strassen beats 3 for the first time: 2.807
- 1981: Schönhage, 2.522
- 1990: Coppersmith-Winograd, 2.376
- 1990 to Aug 2026: 36 years to shave off 0.005, 2.3712
- Nov 2026: OpenAI proves the upper and lower bound is 2.25

Wild to see things we were taught in university be changed right before our very eyes.
title_zh: OpenAI 发布了一份预印本，声称证明矩阵乘法指数 (ω) 恰好是 9/4，解决了数学中的一个重大开放问题
author: Deedy Das
author_role: Menlo Ventures 合伙人 / AI 行业风向观察家
full_text_zh:
OpenAI 刚刚放弃了一个长达 57 年的数学问题的 111 页证明：矩阵乘法指数 (ω) 恰好是 9/4。

该问题在 ProofAtlas 的 500 个数学开放问题中排名第 31，并且可以说在算法中仅次于 P = NP，排名第二。

问题：
两个 n×n 矩阵相乘需要多少步？教科书方法取n^3。真实成本是n^ω。 ω是什么？

历史：
- 1969 年：施特拉森首次击败 3：2.807
- 1981 年：舍恩哈格，2.522
- 1990：铜匠-维诺格勒，2.376
- 1990年至2026年8月：36年削减0.005、2.3712
- 2026 年 11 月：OpenAI 证明上限和下限均为 2.25

很高兴看到我们在大学学到的东西就在我们眼前发生改变。

title_en:
Two extremes in dealing with advances in AI:

1- Convince yourself that AI is (or will become) better than humans at everything. Just surrender to it and forget about learning software engineering, math, science, etc.

2- Strive to learn (including with the help of AI), experiment with the technology, find the areas where AI struggles and human intelligence gives you the edge, deepen your knowledge/skills in specific areas to make you a better user of AI

People who think like (1) will be replaced by people who act like (2)

title: 1. Simulate Realistic User Traffic Testing with a few identical requests won't reveal how your application behaves in production. → Simulate thousands of concurrent users. → Generate different prompt lengths and request types. → Reproduce realistic traffic pa
title_en:
1. Simulate Realistic User Traffic

Testing with a few identical requests won't reveal how your application behaves in production.

→ Simulate thousands of concurrent users.
→ Generate different prompt lengths and request types.
→ Reproduce realistic traffic patterns and usage spikes.
→ Test both normal and peak traffic conditions.

Why it matters: Realistic workloads help uncover bottlenecks that simple performance tests often miss.

Explore: https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/

→ 生成不同的提示长度和请求类型。
→ 再现真实的流量模式和使用峰值。
→ 测试正常和高峰流量条件。

title: 7 Techniques for Testing AI Applications Under Heavy Traffic Your AI application works perfectly with 10 users. But what happens when 10,000 users start sending requests simultaneously? Suddenly, response times increase, GPU resources become saturate
title_en:
7 Techniques for Testing AI Applications Under Heavy Traffic

Your AI application works perfectly with 10 users.

But what happens when 10,000 users start sending requests simultaneously?

Suddenly, response times increase, GPU resources become saturated, API rate limits kick in, and requests start failing.

Traditional load testing isn't always enough for AI applications. You also need to understand token generation, model latency, concurrency, and infrastructure bottlenecks.

Here are 7 techniques for testing AI applications under heavy traffic.
title_zh:
在大流量下测试 AI 应用程序的 7 种技术

您的 AI 应用程序可以与 10 个用户完美配合。

但是，当 10,000 个用户开始同时发送请求时会发生什么？

突然间，响应时间增加，GPU 资源饱和，API 速率限制生效，请求开始失败

title: ▲ ByteDance Seed and HKU researchers just open-sourced Laminar, an RL post-training framework that stops every GPU from waiting on the slowest agent trajectory. The key idea is full decoupling. Rollout, the experience buffer, training and weight sync run
title_en:
▲ ByteDance Seed and HKU researchers just open-sourced Laminar, an RL post-training framework that stops every GPU from waiting on the slowest agent trajectory.

The key idea is full decoupling. Rollout, the experience buffer, training and weight sync run as independent loops. Each trajectory can finish under 1 policy version (version-consistent rollout), so the prefix KV cache is kept and re-prefill is avoided.

On SWE agent RL with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, SWE-bench Verified went from 46.6% to 52.2%, above the 51.4% baseline peak, with 33% fewer trained samples and 64% fewer GPU-hours. It is a trade-off though: the baseline ran on 64x H100 and Laminar on 64x H800 with different batch settings, so the team calls it an end-to-end comparison, not an ablation.

Apache-2.0, built on verl and Uni-Agent, vLLM for inference and Megatron-LM or FSDP2 for training. The paper reports up to 5.48x throughput on 1024 GPUs......

Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/24/bytedance-seed-laminar-async-rl-post-training-framework/

Repo: http://github.com/verl-project/laminar

Paper: http://doi.org/10.1145/3767295.3803580

Blog: http://verl-project.github.io/posts/2026-11-20-laminar/

title: Japan develops AI agent to crack down on anime and manga piracy A 2025 government survey by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs found that 84% of 1,168 suspicious X posts flagged by the AI were illegal. Of 1,564 anime websites flagged, 89% hosted pirat
title_en:
Japan develops AI agent to crack down on anime and manga piracy

A 2025 government survey by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs found that 84% of 1,168 suspicious X posts flagged by the AI were illegal. Of 1,564 anime websites flagged, 89% hosted pirated anime, while 94% of 1,935 flagged manga websites hosted pirated manga

The government plans to expand the AI's detection capabilities to overseas piracy sites, with further findings expected by March 2027. Its broader goal is to direct consumers toward legal platforms and make it easier for copyright holders to combat piracy

日本文化厅 2025 年的一项政府调查发现，人工智能标记的 1,168 个可疑 X 帖子中，84% 是非法的。在 1,564 个被标记的动漫网站中，89% 托管盗版动漫，而在 1,935 个被标记的漫画网站中，94% 托管盗版漫画

政府计划将人工智能的检测能力扩展到海外盗版网站，预计到 2027 年 3 月会有进一步的调查结果。其更广泛的目标是将消费者引导至合法平台，并让者更容易打击盗版

title: This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different
title_en:
This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different levels of output based on how they’ve adopted AI.

This is a different phenomenon from other tech. Typically in the economy you think of technology adoption rates on a per firm basis, because the company generally adopts a relatively standardized approach to doing the new tech thing. Like “that company has gone digital or adopted the cloud”. So generally the uplift across teams is more or less the same across teams. 

AI is starting to look quite different. Even within the same company you can have a 10X delta between the lowest and highest adopters of AI and the impact they’re seeing. The teams that are able to actually figure out how to redesign their processes to best deploy agents in their workflows can see up to an order of magnitude jump in productivity depending on the job function.

Right now this is heavily concentrated in coding, but more work will become coding adjacent so we can expect similar results elsewhere too. This is going to definitely lead to some wild dynamics within companies.

title: Travel writing is in practice some of the best sociology since the naivete of the foreigner grants the permission to make sweeping generalizations and claims that might otherwise seem too poorly-justified to merit publication. “My people have poor manners” is a
title_en:
Travel writing is in practice some of the best sociology since the naivete of the foreigner grants the permission to make sweeping generalizations and claims that might otherwise seem too poorly-justified to merit publication. “My people have poor manners” is a tough claim to credibly land (Who are you? Exactly which life experiences are you drawing on? And what is your agenda in pushing this line of argument?), whereas “on my travels in Scotland, I noticed that the people had poor manners” seems perfectly reasonable, and indeed thought-provoking. Random samples from a distribution help you understand the mean, and the aleatory nature of travel encounters lends credence to the whole assessment.

Alexis de Tocqueville was just 25 when he traveled across the US and 29 when his observations were published. So, Democracy in America is a giant Substack from a young backpacker, written on his peregrinations as he consumed Montesquieu, Pascal, and Rousseau. He was clearly inspired by Montesquieu’s The Spirit of the Laws, which made the case that countries’ governance, and their laws, are necessarily functions of their cultures and manners.

Building on this, Democracy in America is in many ways a “deep roots” work. Tocqueville is emphatic (at times comically so) that it is America's culture that explains its success, and that its culture in turn stems from the country’s initial conditions. “I think I can see the whole destiny of America contained in the first Puritan who landed on those shores.” He thinks it's important that New England was settled by “a greater mass of intelligence than is to be found in any European nation of our own time” who brought the “best elements of order and morality”. He points out that Mexico doesn’t work nearly as well, despite copying the American constitution and laws, and notes disapprovingly that Virginia was founded by gold-seeking people “without character” whose “turbulent spirit [...] endangered the infant colony.” At the end of Volume I, he concludes, practically table-thumping: “If in the course of this work I have not succeeded in making the reader feel the importance that I attribute to the practical experience of the Americans, to their habits, to their opinions, in a word, to their moeurs, in maintaining their laws, I have failed in the principal object that I proposed to myself in writing it.”

We could look at Democracy in America as an early work of development economics: he is attempting to systematically figure out why it is that America works. (And not just out of casual interest: he was a member of an aristocratic family that was entangled with recent French political upheaval.) By placing primacy on culture, Tocqueville’s explanation deviates from the institutional and structural explanations often favored by today’s economists. Daron Acemoglu, to choose one prominent present-day example, firmly rejects the “Culture Hypothesis” in Why Nations Fail. In explaining Virginia, he instead points to structural incentives. Poor Economics, from Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee, contains a similar rejection of cultural explanations. Comparable examples from other leading economists abound. An aversion to cultural explanations is of course understandable for all sorts of reasons: cultures are opaque, protean, and resistant to quantitative characterization. Cultures are themselves shaped by other factors, such that it’s hard to attribute definitive causality, and it’s uncomfortable to adopt anything that feels like a normative orientation. Nonetheless, can we explain why New England differs from Mexico without starting with the inner disposition, habits, and worldviews of the people? Tocqueville thinks not.

For all culture’s importance, it would be wrong to suggest that Tocqueville believes that culture is the only factor that matters. He dwells extensively on how America’s institutions are important, and how the microstructure of town life shapes the country’s federal civics. It is also true that development economics has taken a more strongly cultural turn in recent times, most of all in Joel Mokyr’s 2025 Nobel Prize. Mokyr’s work feels downright Tocquevillian at times: contra the intimidatingly quantitative econometrics that dominates today, Mokyr engages in an extended and earnestly curious qualitative synthesis of relevant patterns (in his case, in service of trying to figure out why the Industrial Revolution started when it did). Like Tocqueville, he concludes that the best explanation places cultural changes above other factors.

I’m very interested in whether LLMs will help us characterize culture in new and at least somewhat more objective ways. Can we ingest and process vast quantities of work that may not even have been OCR’d or translated until now? Can we map cultural corpora to vectors in some foundation model embedding space? Where large datasets and computational techniques enabled new ways to analyze many economic questions in recent decades, perhaps LLMs will enable newly objective light to be shone on hypothesized cultural explanations.

–

Speaking of LLMs, Democracy in America is a book about a new kind of society, and a Frenchman trying to figure out what the future might hold. As we sit on the cusp of another upheaval, is there anything that reads with resonance today?

Part of the declared promise of AI is that it might obviate our need to work. In slavery, Tocqueville observes a version of this phenomenon on his travels. He is struck by its barbarous cruelty (and his travel companion later published an anti-slavery novel), but also by its effects on the slaveowners themselves. He perceived that the practice rendered work dishonorable, and thus yielded idleness, ignorance, and pride. Slavery, he says, “enervates the powers of the mind, and benumbs the activity of man.” He observes the contrast between slavery-rejecting Ohio and slavery-embracing Kentucky. In Kentucky, “those who are active and enlightened either do nothing or pass over into the State of Ohio, where they may work without dishonor.” Ohio’s harvests are more abundant, homes are more elegant, and people seem to be “in enjoyment of that wealth and contentment which is the reward of labor.”

Presented with an evil release from manual labor, the Kentuckians did not apply themselves to productive studies and great creations, and the South did not become a new Florence. There is an obvious question for us: how will AI change our relationship with work? Will it become dishonorable, and what will the reflexive effect on our society be if so? Should this change our view of utopian visions of “automated communism”?

Tocqueville also raises the issue of coexistence with more advanced neighbors. He noted that the arrival of the Europeans had been ruinous for the Indians (as he termed them). European technology – firearms, metallurgy, steam power – was a kind of superintelligence relative to their practices. The disruptions and destruction wrought by the settlers led to cultural problems (“their traditions obscured, and the chain of their recollections broken”), which in turn led to declines in both the physical and the moral conditions of the tribes. Tocqueville believed that the Indians faced a choice given that their old way of living was no longer viable: they could adopt European mores or suffer inevitable destruction. He predicted that they would reject cultural adaptation, and thus were “doomed to perish”. This is all to say that the arrival of the European settlers was in Tocqueville’s eyes injurious to the Indians not only because of the direct violence and displacement, but also because the contact was itself so disruptive to their societies that their cultures ceased to function. Some of this was later observed in Pacific island societies – even though there wasn’t the same degree of violent dispossession, the mere presence of Western contact was intrinsically destabilizing. In many visions of the future, superintelligent AIs are much more numerous than humans, with consequences that are hard to predict. In Tocqueville, there is a cautionary suggestion.

Given the new powers afforded by AI, there is a question of what we will choose to do with it – to the extent that we are in control, we will wield a vastly expanded authority. Americans faced some version of this question: in democracy, society was endowed with wholly new ways to express its collective will, with no ultimate superior power, for society was for the first time in charge of itself. Tocqueville repeatedly emphasizes how democracy thus increased the importance of religion as a regulator of hasty or unwise impulses. “Whilst the law permits the Americans to do what they please, religion prevents them from conceiving, and forbids them to commit, what is rash or unjust.” If we take seriously Tocqueville’s idea that religion was a critical complement in ensuring that people shaped societies in prudent ways, Democracy implicitly raises a question: which are the ideas, philosophies, religions, or doctrines that will help us wield AI well?

Part of what’s interesting and memorable about the work is Tocqueville’s combination of curiosity, enthusiasm, and slight ambivalence about democracy itself. He grants that democracy is likely to be the future of governance, and he is admiring of what it has achieved in America, but he can’t avoid concerns about what it may augur (such as the unchecked and totalitarian impulses of the mob). At the end of Volume II, he describes his chief concern with democracy: that it may yield a new form of despotism that he struggles to define. He fears not tyrants, but, he says, “guardians”. He is worried about a world where:

> Above this race of men stands an immense and tutelary power, which takes upon itself alone to secure their gratifications, and to watch over their fate. [...] It would be like the authority of a parent, if, like that authority, its object was to prepare men for manhood; but it seeks on the contrary to keep them in perpetual childhood: it is well content that the people should rejoice, provided they think of nothing but rejoicing. For their happiness such a government willingly labors, but it chooses to be the sole agent and the only arbiter of that happiness. [...] What remains, but to spare them all the care of thinking and all the trouble of living? Thus it every day renders the exercise of the free agency of man less useful and less frequent; it circumscribes the will within a narrower range, and gradually robs a man of all the uses of himself.

The Iain Banks Culture novels are often invoked by AI proponents. For Tocqueville, something strikingly like the world that they describe was his dystopian fear, for a world bereft of autonomy would be intrinsically degrading and humiliating for humanity:

> The will of man is not shattered, but softened, bent, and guided: men are seldom forced by it to act, but they are constantly restrained from acting: such a power does not destroy, but it prevents existence; it does not tyrannize, but it compresses, enervates, extinguishes, and stupefies a people, till each nation is reduced to be nothing better than a flock of timid and industrious animals, of which the government is the shepherd.

The analogy to animals is noteworthy. In interviews, AI leaders occasionally analogize the future human state to that of pets. Banks himself noted that in the Culture novels, “[humans] have a status somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.” In Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace, he hopes that humans are “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”.

Tocqueville at heart thought that agency and cultivation of people came above all else. He dreaded anesthetized placidity. In soft despotism, he feared that “ambition will lose its vigor and its greatness; that human passions will be appeased and lowered at the same time”. This vigor was for Tocqueville at the heart of what was admirable in America, whose bustle and intensity he repeatedly extols. American self-reliance and self-direction are paramount: “the citizen of the United States is taught from his earliest infancy to rely upon his own exertions in order to resist the evils and the difficulties of life.” For Tocqueville, any kind of servile and manicured comfort was not just undesirable, but a negation of the American promise.

Many of the Elysian visions for AI hinge on AI resolving the messy coordination challenges that afflict humans. (Scott Alexander invokes this vision towards the end of Meditations on Moloch.) For Tocqueville, the arbitration of such differences was precisely the constructive activity that reaffirmed our agency. Townships, juries, associations, and their attendant squabbles are how culture is reinforced and how judgment is cultivated. When a town decides whether to fund a school, there are two outputs: a decision, and practice in governance itself. If AI could resolve such matters, we might get better outcomes, but will we get better people?
title_zh: 旅行写作实际上是最好的社会学之一，因为外国人的天真允许他们做出全面的概括和主张，否则这些概括和主张可能看起来缺乏合理性，不值得发表。 “我的人民没有礼貌”是一个很难获得可信土地的说法（你是谁？你到底借鉴了哪些生活经历？你推动这一论点的议程是
author: @patrickc
summary_zh:
什么？），而“在我在苏格兰的旅行中，我注意到人们没有礼貌”似乎完全合理，而且确实发人深省。分布中的随机样本可帮助您了解平均值，而旅行遭遇的偶然性则为整个评估提供了可信度。

亚历克西斯·德·托克维尔 (Alexis de Tocqueville) 穿越美国时年仅 25 岁，发表观察结果时年仅 29 岁。所以，《美国的民主》是一位年轻背包客写的一个巨大的子堆栈，写的是他在阅读孟德斯鸠、帕斯卡和卢梭时的旅行经历。他显然受到了孟德斯鸠的《法律精神》的启发，该书认为国家的治理及其法律必然是其文化和行为方式的功能。

在此基础上，《美国的民主》在很多方面都是一部“根深蒂固”的作品。托克维尔强调（有时是滑稽的），美国的文化解释了它的成功，而它的文化又源于这个国家的初始条件。 “我想我可以看到美国的整个命运包含在第一个登陆这些海岸的清教徒身上。”他认为，重要的是，新英格兰的定居者“比我们这个时代的任何欧洲国家都拥有更多的智慧”，他们带来了“秩序和道德的最佳要素”。他指出，尽管抄袭了美国宪法和法律，但墨西哥的运作情况却差强人意，他不以为然地指出，弗吉尼亚是由“没有品格”的淘金者建立的，他们的“狂暴精神……危及了刚刚诞生的殖民地”。在第一卷的结尾，他几乎是震撼地总结道：“如果在这部作品的过程中，我没有成功地让读者感受到我赋予美国人的实践经验、他们的习惯、他们的观点，总之，他们的摩尔和维护他们的法律的重要性，那么我就没有实现我在写这本书时向自己提出的主要目标。”

我们可以将《美国的民主》视为发展经济学的早期著作：他试图系统地找出美国运转的原因。 （不仅仅是出于偶然的兴趣：他是一个与最近的法国政治动荡纠缠在一起的贵族家庭的成员。）通过将文化置于首位，托克维尔的解释偏离了当今经济学家通常青睐的制度和结构解释。达龙·阿塞莫格鲁（Daron Acemoglu）选择当今一个著名的例子，坚决拒绝《国家为何失败》中的“文化假设”。在解释弗吉尼亚州时，他转而指出了结构性激励措施。埃丝特·迪弗洛和阿比吉特·班纳吉的《贫穷经济学》也包含了对文化解释的类似拒绝。其他领先经济学家的类似例子比比皆是。由于各种原因，对文化解释的厌恶当然是可以理解的：文化是不透明的、千变万化的，并且抵制定量表征。文化本身是由其他因素塑造的，因此很难归因于明确的因果关系，并且采用任何感觉像是规范取向的东西都会让人感到不舒服。尽管如此，我们能否在不从人们的内在性格、习惯和世界观出发的情况下解释为什么新英格兰与墨西哥不同呢？托克维尔认为不是。

尽管文化很重要，但如果认为托克维尔认为文化是唯一重要的因素，那就错了。他详细阐述了美国机构的重要性，以及城镇生活的微观结构如何塑造该国的联邦公民制度。发展经济学近年来也确实发生了更强烈的文化转向，尤其是乔尔·莫克尔 (Joel Mokyr) 获得 2025 年诺贝尔奖。莫基尔的作品有时给人一种彻头彻尾的托克维尔式的感觉：与当今占主导地位的令人生畏的定量计量经济学相反，莫基尔对相关模式进行了广泛而真诚的定性综合（在他的例子中，是为了试图找出工业革命为何在此时开始）。和托克维尔一样，他得出的结论是，最好的解释是将文化变化置于其他因素之上。

我对法学硕士是否能帮助我们以新的、至少更客观的方式描述文化非常感兴趣。我们能否摄取和处理大量迄今为止可能尚未进行 OCR 或翻译的工作？我们可以将文化语料库映射到某些基础模型嵌入空间中的向量吗？近几十年来，大型数据集和计算技术为分析许多经济问题提供了新的方法，也许法学硕士将为假设的文化解释提供新的客观视角。

–

说到法学硕士，《美国的民主》是一本关于新型社会的书，讲述的是一个法国人试图弄清楚未来会怎样。当我们正处于另一场剧变的风口浪尖时，今天有什么东西读起来能引起共鸣吗？

人工智能所宣称的部分承诺是它可能会消除我们工作的需要。在奴隶制中，托克维尔在他的旅行中观察到了这种现象的一个版本。他对其野蛮的残忍感到震惊（他的旅伴后来出版了一本反奴隶制小说），但也对其对奴隶主本身的影响感到震惊。他认为这种做法使工作变得不光彩，从而导致懒惰、无知和骄傲。他说，奴隶制“削弱了思想的力量，麻木了人类的活动”。他观察了拒绝奴隶制的俄亥俄州和拥护奴隶制的肯塔基州之间的对比。在肯塔基州，“那些积极主动、开明的人要么什么也不做，要么就转到俄亥俄州，在那里他们可以毫无耻辱地工作。”俄亥俄州的收成更加丰富，房屋更加优雅，人们似乎“享受着劳动的回报所带来的财富和满足”。

肯塔基人从体力劳动中得到了邪恶的释放，他们没有致力于富有成效的研究和伟大的创造，南方也没有成为新的佛罗伦萨。我们面临一个显而易见的问题：人工智能将如何改变我们与工作的关系？它会变得不光彩吗？如果是的话，会对我们的社会产生什么反射性影响？这是否应该改变我们对“自动化共产主义”乌托邦愿景的看法？

托克维尔还提出了与更先进的邻国共存的问题。他指出，欧洲人的到来对印第安人（他是这样称呼他们的）来说是毁灭性的。欧洲技术——火器、冶金、蒸汽动力——相对于他们的实践来说是一种超级智能。定居者造成的破坏和破坏导致了文化问题（“他们的传统被模糊了，他们的记忆链被打破了”），这反过来又导致了部落的物质和道德状况的下降。托克维尔认为，鉴于印第安人旧有的生活方式不再可行，他们面临着一个选择：他们要么接受欧洲的习俗，要么遭受不可避免的毁灭。他预测他们会拒绝文化适应，因此“注定要灭亡”。这就是说，在托克维尔看来，欧洲定居者的到来对印第安人造成了伤害，不仅因为直接的暴力和流离失所，而且因为这种接触本身对他们的社会造成了如此大的破坏，以至于他们的文化停止了运作。后来在太平洋岛屿社会中观察到了其中的一些情况——尽管没有同等程度的暴力剥夺，但西方接触的存在本质上是不稳定的。在未来的许多愿景中，超级智能人工智能的数量比人类多得多，其后果难以预测。托克维尔有一个警告性的建议。

鉴于人工智能提供的新权力，存在一个问题，即我们将选择如何利用它——在我们能够控制的范围内，我们将拥有极大扩展的权力。美国人面临着这个问题的某种版本：在民主制度下，社会被赋予了全新的方式来表达其集体意志，没有最终的超级权力，因为社会第一次掌握了自己。托克维尔反复强调，民主如何增强了宗教作为调节草率或不明智冲动的作用的重要性。 “虽然法律允许美国人做他们想做的事，但宗教却阻止他们怀孕，并禁止他们做出鲁莽或不公正的事情。”如果我们认真对待托克维尔的观点，即宗教是确保人们以审慎方式塑造社会的关键补充，那么民主就隐含地提出了一个问题：哪些思想、哲学、宗教或教义将帮助我们很好地运用人工智能？

这部作品的有趣和令人难忘的部分原因在于托克维尔对民主本身的好奇、热情和轻微的矛盾心理的结合。他承认民主很可能是治理的未来，他对民主在美国取得的成就表示钦佩，但他无法避免对其可能预示的事情的担忧（例如暴民不受控制的极权主义冲动）。在第二卷的结尾，他描述了他对民主的主要担忧：民主可能会产生一种他努力定义的新形式的专制主义。他说，他害怕的不是暴君，而是“守护者”。他担心这样一个世界：

> 在这个人类种族之上矗立着一种巨大的守护力量，它独自承担起确保他们的满足并守护他们的命运的责任。 [...] 如果像父母的权威一样，它的目的是让男人为成年做准备，那么它就像父母的权威一样；但它的目的恰恰相反，让他们永远处于童年状态：人民应该感到高兴，只要他们只想到高兴，它就很满足了。为了他们的幸福，这样的政府愿意努力工作，但它选择成为这种幸福的唯一代理人和唯一仲裁者。 [...]除了让他们免去思考的烦恼和生活的烦恼之外，还剩下什么？因此，人的自由意志的行使日益变得不那么有用，也越来越不频繁。它把意志限制在一个更窄的范围内，并逐渐剥夺一个人对自己的一切用处。

人工智能支持者经常引用伊恩·班克斯的文化小说。对于托克维尔来说，与他们所描述的世界惊人相似的是他的反乌托邦恐惧，因为一个失去自治的世界本质上是对人类的侮辱和羞辱：

> 人的意志不是被粉碎，而是被软化、弯曲和引导：人很少被它强迫去行动，而是不断地被限制去行动：这样的力量不会毁灭，但它阻止存在；它不是暴政，而是压迫、削弱、消灭和麻痹人民，直到每个国家沦为一群胆怯而勤劳的动物，而政府就是它们的牧羊人。

与动物的类比值得注意。在采访中，人工智能领导者偶尔会将未来人类的状态与宠物的状态进行类比。班克斯本人指出，在文化小说中，“[人类]的地位介于乘客、宠物和寄生虫之间。”在理查德·布劳蒂根（Richard Brautigan）的著名诗《一切都被慈爱的机器守护着》中，他希望人类“回到我们的哺乳动物兄弟姐妹身边”。

托克维尔内心认为，人的能动性和修养高于一切。他害怕麻醉般的平静。在软专制下，他担心“野心将失去活力和伟大；人类的激情将同时被平息和降低”。对托克维尔来说，这种活力是美国令人钦佩的事物的核心，他一再赞扬美国的喧嚣和强度。美国人的自力更生和自我指导至关重要：“美国公民从小就被教导要依靠自己的努力来抵抗生活中的邪恶和困难。”对于托克维尔来说，任何形式的奴性和精心设计的舒适不仅是不可取的，而且是对美国承诺的否定。

人工智能的许多极乐愿景都依赖于人工智能解决困扰人类的混乱协调挑战。 （斯科特·亚历山大在《摩洛沉思录》的结尾处引用了这一愿景。）对于托克维尔来说，对这些分歧的仲裁恰恰是重申我们能动性的建设性活动。乡镇、陪审团、协会以及随之而来的争吵是文化得以强化、判断力得以培养的方式。当一个城镇决定是否资助一所学校时，有两个产出：决策和治理本身的实践。如果人工智能能够解决这些问题，我们可能会得到更好的结果，但我们会得到更好的人吗？

full_text_en:
Travel writing is in practice some of the best sociology since the naivete of the foreigner grants the permission to make sweeping generalizations and claims that might otherwise seem too poorly-justified to merit publication. “My people have poor manners” is a tough claim to credibly land (Who are you? Exactly which life experiences are you drawing on? And what is your agenda in pushing this line of argument?), whereas “on my travels in Scotland, I noticed that the people had poor manners” seems perfectly reasonable, and indeed thought-provoking. Random samples from a distribution help you understand the mean, and the aleatory nature of travel encounters lends credence to the whole assessment.

Alexis de Tocqueville was just 25 when he traveled across the US and 29 when his observations were published. So, Democracy in America is a giant Substack from a young backpacker, written on his peregrinations as he consumed Montesquieu, Pascal, and Rousseau. He was clearly inspired by Montesquieu’s The Spirit of the Laws, which made the case that countries’ governance, and their laws, are necessarily functions of their cultures and manners.

Building on this, Democracy in America is in many ways a “deep roots” work. Tocqueville is emphatic (at times comically so) that it is America's culture that explains its success, and that its culture in turn stems from the country’s initial conditions. “I think I can see the whole destiny of America contained in the first Puritan who landed on those shores.” He thinks it's important that New England was settled by “a greater mass of intelligence than is to be found in any European nation of our own time” who brought the “best elements of order and morality”. He points out that Mexico doesn’t work nearly as well, despite copying the American constitution and laws, and notes disapprovingly that Virginia was founded by gold-seeking people “without character” whose “turbulent spirit [...] endangered the infant colony.” At the end of Volume I, he concludes, practically table-thumping: “If in the course of this work I have not succeeded in making the reader feel the importance that I attribute to the practical experience of the Americans, to their habits, to their opinions, in a word, to their moeurs, in maintaining their laws, I have failed in the principal object that I proposed to myself in writing it.”

We could look at Democracy in America as an early work of development economics: he is attempting to systematically figure out why it is that America works. (And not just out of casual interest: he was a member of an aristocratic family that was entangled with recent French political upheaval.) By placing primacy on culture, Tocqueville’s explanation deviates from the institutional and structural explanations often favored by today’s economists. Daron Acemoglu, to choose one prominent present-day example, firmly rejects the “Culture Hypothesis” in Why Nations Fail. In explaining Virginia, he instead points to structural incentives. Poor Economics, from Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee, contains a similar rejection of cultural explanations. Comparable examples from other leading economists abound. An aversion to cultural explanations is of course understandable for all sorts of reasons: cultures are opaque, protean, and resistant to quantitative characterization. Cultures are themselves shaped by other factors, such that it’s hard to attribute definitive causality, and it’s uncomfortable to adopt anything that feels like a normative orientation. Nonetheless, can we explain why New England differs from Mexico without starting with the inner disposition, habits, and worldviews of the people? Tocqueville thinks not.

For all culture’s importance, it would be wrong to suggest that Tocqueville believes that culture is the only factor that matters. He dwells extensively on how America’s institutions are important, and how the microstructure of town life shapes the country’s federal civics. It is also true that development economics has taken a more strongly cultural turn in recent times, most of all in Joel Mokyr’s 2025 Nobel Prize. Mokyr’s work feels downright Tocquevillian at times: contra the intimidatingly quantitative econometrics that dominates today, Mokyr engages in an extended and earnestly curious qualitative synthesis of relevant patterns (in his case, in service of trying to figure out why the Industrial Revolution started when it did). Like Tocqueville, he concludes that the best explanation places cultural changes above other factors.

I’m very interested in whether LLMs will help us characterize culture in new and at least somewhat more objective ways. Can we ingest and process vast quantities of work that may not even have been OCR’d or translated until now? Can we map cultural corpora to vectors in some foundation model embedding space? Where large datasets and computational techniques enabled new ways to analyze many economic questions in recent decades, perhaps LLMs will enable newly objective light to be shone on hypothesized cultural explanations.

–

Speaking of LLMs, Democracy in America is a book about a new kind of society, and a Frenchman trying to figure out what the future might hold. As we sit on the cusp of another upheaval, is there anything that reads with resonance today?

Part of the declared promise of AI is that it might obviate our need to work. In slavery, Tocqueville observes a version of this phenomenon on his travels. He is struck by its barbarous cruelty (and his travel companion later published an anti-slavery novel), but also by its effects on the slaveowners themselves. He perceived that the practice rendered work dishonorable, and thus yielded idleness, ignorance, and pride. Slavery, he says, “enervates the powers of the mind, and benumbs the activity of man.” He observes the contrast between slavery-rejecting Ohio and slavery-embracing Kentucky. In Kentucky, “those who are active and enlightened either do nothing or pass over into the State of Ohio, where they may work without dishonor.” Ohio’s harvests are more abundant, homes are more elegant, and people seem to be “in enjoyment of that wealth and contentment which is the reward of labor.”

Presented with an evil release from manual labor, the Kentuckians did not apply themselves to productive studies and great creations, and the South did not become a new Florence. There is an obvious question for us: how will AI change our relationship with work? Will it become dishonorable, and what will the reflexive effect on our society be if so? Should this change our view of utopian visions of “automated communism”?

Tocqueville also raises the issue of coexistence with more advanced neighbors. He noted that the arrival of the Europeans had been ruinous for the Indians (as he termed them). European technology – firearms, metallurgy, steam power – was a kind of superintelligence relative to their practices. The disruptions and destruction wrought by the settlers led to cultural problems (“their traditions obscured, and the chain of their recollections broken”), which in turn led to declines in both the physical and the moral conditions of the tribes. Tocqueville believed that the Indians faced a choice given that their old way of living was no longer viable: they could adopt European mores or suffer inevitable destruction. He predicted that they would reject cultural adaptation, and thus were “doomed to perish”. This is all to say that the arrival of the European settlers was in Tocqueville’s eyes injurious to the Indians not only because of the direct violence and displacement, but also because the contact was itself so disruptive to their societies that their cultures ceased to function. Some of this was later observed in Pacific island societies – even though there wasn’t the same degree of violent dispossession, the mere presence of Western contact was intrinsically destabilizing. In many visions of the future, superintelligent AIs are much more numerous than humans, with consequences that are hard to predict. In Tocqueville, there is a cautionary suggestion.

Given the new powers afforded by AI, there is a question of what we will choose to do with it – to the extent that we are in control, we will wield a vastly expanded authority. Americans faced some version of this question: in democracy, society was endowed with wholly new ways to express its collective will, with no ultimate superior power, for society was for the first time in charge of itself. Tocqueville repeatedly emphasizes how democracy thus increased the importance of religion as a regulator of hasty or unwise impulses. “Whilst the law permits the Americans to do what they please, religion prevents them from conceiving, and forbids them to commit, what is rash or unjust.” If we take seriously Tocqueville’s idea that religion was a critical complement in ensuring that people shaped societies in prudent ways, Democracy implicitly raises a question: which are the ideas, philosophies, religions, or doctrines that will help us wield AI well?

Part of what’s interesting and memorable about the work is Tocqueville’s combination of curiosity, enthusiasm, and slight ambivalence about democracy itself. He grants that democracy is likely to be the future of governance, and he is admiring of what it has achieved in America, but he can’t avoid concerns about what it may augur (such as the unchecked and totalitarian impulses of the mob). At the end of Volume II, he describes his chief concern with democracy: that it may yield a new form of despotism that he struggles to define. He fears not tyrants, but, he says, “guardians”. He is worried about a world where:

> Above this race of men stands an immense and tutelary power, which takes upon itself alone to secure their gratifications, and to watch over their fate. [...] It would be like the authority of a parent, if, like that authority, its object was to prepare men for manhood; but it seeks on the contrary to keep them in perpetual childhood: it is well content that the people should rejoice, provided they think of nothing but rejoicing. For their happiness such a government willingly labors, but it chooses to be the sole agent and the only arbiter of that happiness. [...] What remains, but to spare them all the care of thinking and all the trouble of living? Thus it every day renders the exercise of the free agency of man less useful and less frequent; it circumscribes the will within a narrower range, and gradually robs a man of all the uses of himself.

The Iain Banks Culture novels are often invoked by AI proponents. For Tocqueville, something strikingly like the world that they describe was his dystopian fear, for a world bereft of autonomy would be intrinsically degrading and humiliating for humanity:

> The will of man is not shattered, but softened, bent, and guided: men are seldom forced by it to act, but they are constantly restrained from acting: such a power does not destroy, but it prevents existence; it does not tyrannize, but it compresses, enervates, extinguishes, and stupefies a people, till each nation is reduced to be nothing better than a flock of timid and industrious animals, of which the government is the shepherd.

The analogy to animals is noteworthy. In interviews, AI leaders occasionally analogize the future human state to that of pets. Banks himself noted that in the Culture novels, “[humans] have a status somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.” In Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace, he hopes that humans are “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”.

Tocqueville at heart thought that agency and cultivation of people came above all else. He dreaded anesthetized placidity. In soft despotism, he feared that “ambition will lose its vigor and its greatness; that human passions will be appeased and lowered at the same time”. This vigor was for Tocqueville at the heart of what was admirable in America, whose bustle and intensity he repeatedly extols. American self-reliance and self-direction are paramount: “the citizen of the United States is taught from his earliest infancy to rely upon his own exertions in order to resist the evils and the difficulties of life.” For Tocqueville, any kind of servile and manicured comfort was not just undesirable, but a negation of the American promise.

Many of the Elysian visions for AI hinge on AI resolving the messy coordination challenges that afflict humans. (Scott Alexander invokes this vision towards the end of Meditations on Moloch.) For Tocqueville, the arbitration of such differences was precisely the constructive activity that reaffirmed our agency. Townships, juries, associations, and their attendant squabbles are how culture is reinforced and how judgment is cultivated. When a town decides whether to fund a school, there are two outputs: a decision, and practice in governance itself. If AI could resolve such matters, we might get better outcomes, but will we get better people?

旅行写作实际上是最好的社会学之一，因为外国人的天真允许他们做出全面的概括和主张，否则这些概括和主张可能看起来缺乏合理性，不值得发表。 “我的人民没有礼貌”是一个很难获得可信土地的说法（你是谁？你到底借鉴了哪些生活经历？你推动这一论点的议程是什么？），而“在我在苏格兰的旅行中，我注意到人们没有礼貌”似乎完全合理，而且确实发人深省。分布中的随机样本可帮助您了解平均值，而旅行遭遇的偶然性则为整个评估提供了可信度。

亚历克西斯·德·托克维尔 (Alexis de Tocqueville) 穿越美国时年仅 25 岁，发表观察结果时年仅 29 岁。所以，《美国的民主》是一位年轻背包客写的一个巨大的子堆栈，写的是他在阅读孟德斯鸠、帕斯卡和卢梭时的旅行经历。他显然受到了孟德斯鸠的《法律精神》的启发，该书认为国家的治理及其法律必然是其文化和行为方式的功能。

在此基础上，《美国的民主》在很多方面都是一部“根深蒂固”的作品。托克维尔强调（有时是滑稽的），美国的文化解释了它的成功，而它的文化又源于这个国家的初始条件。 “我想我可以看到美国的整个命运包含在第一个登陆这些海岸的清教徒身上。”他认为，重要的是，新英格兰的定居者“比我们这个时代的任何欧洲国家都拥有更多的智慧”，他们带来了“秩序和道德的最佳要素”。他指出，尽管抄袭了美国宪法和法律，但墨西哥的运作情况却差强人意，他不以为然地指出，弗吉尼亚是由“没有品格”的淘金者建立的，他们的“狂暴精神……危及了刚刚诞生的殖民地”。在第一卷的结尾，他几乎是震撼地总结道：“如果在这部作品的过程中，我没有成功地让读者感受到我赋予美国人的实践经验、他们的习惯、他们的观点，总之，他们的摩尔和维护他们的法律的重要性，那么我就没有实现我在写这本书时向自己提出的主要目标。”

我们可以将《美国的民主》视为发展经济学的早期著作：他试图系统地找出美国运转的原因。 （不仅仅是出于偶然的兴趣：他是一个与最近的法国政治动荡纠缠在一起的贵族家庭的成员。）通过将文化置于首位，托克维尔的解释偏离了当今经济学家通常青睐的制度和结构解释。达龙·阿塞莫格鲁（Daron Acemoglu）选择当今一个著名的例子，坚决拒绝《国家为何失败》中的“文化假设”。在解释弗吉尼亚州时，他转而指出了结构性激励措施。埃丝特·迪弗洛和阿比吉特·班纳吉的《贫穷经济学》也包含了对文化解释的类似拒绝。其他领先经济学家的类似例子比比皆是。由于各种原因，对文化解释的厌恶当然是可以理解的：文化是不透明的、千变万化的，并且抵制定量表征。文化本身是由其他因素塑造的，因此很难归因于明确的因果关系，并且采用任何感觉像是规范取向的东西都会让人感到不舒服。尽管如此，我们能否在不从人们的内在性格、习惯和世界观出发的情况下解释为什么新英格兰与墨西哥不同呢？托克维尔认为不是。

尽管文化很重要，但如果认为托克维尔认为文化是唯一重要的因素，那就错了。他详细阐述了美国机构的重要性，以及城镇生活的微观结构如何塑造该国的联邦公民制度。发展经济学近年来也确实发生了更强烈的文化转向，尤其是乔尔·莫克尔 (Joel Mokyr) 获得 2025 年诺贝尔奖。莫基尔的作品有时给人一种彻头彻尾的托克维尔式的感觉：与当今占主导地位的令人生畏的定量计量经济学相反，莫基尔对相关模式进行了广泛而真诚的定性综合（在他的例子中，是为了试图找出工业革命为何在此时开始）。和托克维尔一样，他得出的结论是，最好的解释是将文化变化置于其他因素之上。

我对法学硕士是否能帮助我们以新的、至少更客观的方式描述文化非常感兴趣。我们能否摄取和处理大量迄今为止可能尚未进行 OCR 或翻译的工作？我们可以将文化语料库映射到某些基础模型嵌入空间中的向量吗？近几十年来，大型数据集和计算技术为分析许多经济问题提供了新的方法，也许法学硕士将为假设的文化解释提供新的客观视角。

–

说到法学硕士，《美国的民主》是一本关于新型社会的书，讲述的是一个法国人试图弄清楚未来会怎样。当我们正处于另一场剧变的风口浪尖时，今天有什么东西读起来能引起共鸣吗？

人工智能所宣称的部分承诺是它可能会消除我们工作的需要。在奴隶制中，托克维尔在他的旅行中观察到了这种现象的一个版本。他对其野蛮的残忍感到震惊（他的旅伴后来出版了一本反奴隶制小说），但也对其对奴隶主本身的影响感到震惊。他认为这种做法使工作变得不光彩，从而导致懒惰、无知和骄傲。他说，奴隶制“削弱了思想的力量，麻木了人类的活动”。他观察了拒绝奴隶制的俄亥俄州和拥护奴隶制的肯塔基州之间的对比。在肯塔基州，“那些积极主动、开明的人要么什么也不做，要么就转到俄亥俄州，在那里他们可以毫无耻辱地工作。”俄亥俄州的收成更加丰富，房屋更加优雅，人们似乎“享受着劳动的回报所带来的财富和满足”。

肯塔基人从体力劳动中得到了邪恶的释放，他们没有致力于富有成效的研究和伟大的创造，南方也没有成为新的佛罗伦萨。我们面临一个显而易见的问题：人工智能将如何改变我们与工作的关系？它会变得不光彩吗？如果是的话，会对我们的社会产生什么反射性影响？这是否应该改变我们对“自动化共产主义”乌托邦愿景的看法？

托克维尔还提出了与更先进的邻国共存的问题。他指出，欧洲人的到来对印第安人（他是这样称呼他们的）来说是毁灭性的。欧洲技术——火器、冶金、蒸汽动力——相对于他们的实践来说是一种超级智能。定居者造成的破坏和破坏导致了文化问题（“他们的传统被模糊了，他们的记忆链被打破了”），这反过来又导致了部落的物质和道德状况的下降。托克维尔认为，鉴于印第安人旧有的生活方式不再可行，他们面临着一个选择：他们要么接受欧洲的习俗，要么遭受不可避免的毁灭。他预测他们会拒绝文化适应，因此“注定要灭亡”。这就是说，在托克维尔看来，欧洲定居者的到来对印第安人造成了伤害，不仅因为直接的暴力和流离失所，而且因为这种接触本身对他们的社会造成了如此大的破坏，以至于他们的文化停止了运作。后来在太平洋岛屿社会中观察到了其中的一些情况——尽管没有同等程度的暴力剥夺，但西方接触的存在本质上是不稳定的。在未来的许多愿景中，超级智能人工智能的数量比人类多得多，其后果难以预测。托克维尔有一个警告性的建议。

鉴于人工智能提供的新权力，存在一个问题，即我们将选择如何利用它——在我们能够控制的范围内，我们将拥有极大扩展的权力。美国人面临着这个问题的某种版本：在民主制度下，社会被赋予了全新的方式来表达其集体意志，没有最终的超级权力，因为社会第一次掌握了自己。托克维尔反复强调，民主如何增强了宗教作为调节草率或不明智冲动的作用的重要性。 “虽然法律允许美国人做他们想做的事，但宗教却阻止他们怀孕，并禁止他们做出鲁莽或不公正的事情。”如果我们认真对待托克维尔的观点，即宗教是确保人们以审慎方式塑造社会的关键补充，那么民主就隐含地提出了一个问题：哪些思想、哲学、宗教或教义将帮助我们很好地运用人工智能？

这部作品的有趣和令人难忘的部分原因在于托克维尔对民主本身的好奇、热情和轻微的矛盾心理的结合。他承认民主很可能是治理的未来，他对民主在美国取得的成就表示钦佩，但他无法避免对其可能预示的事情的担忧（例如暴民不受控制的极权主义冲动）。在第二卷的结尾，他描述了他对民主的主要担忧：民主可能会产生一种他努力定义的新形式的专制主义。他说，他害怕的不是暴君，而是“守护者”。他担心这样一个世界：

> 在这个人类种族之上矗立着一种巨大的守护力量，它独自承担起确保他们的满足并守护他们的命运的责任。 [...] 如果像父母的权威一样，它的目的是让男人为成年做准备，那么它就像父母的权威一样；但它的目的恰恰相反，让他们永远处于童年状态：人民应该感到高兴，只要他们只想到高兴，它就很满足了。为了他们的幸福，这样的政府愿意努力工作，但它选择成为这种幸福的唯一代理人和唯一仲裁者。 [...]除了让他们免去思考的烦恼和生活的烦恼之外，还剩下什么？因此，人的自由意志的行使日益变得不那么有用，也越来越不频繁。它把意志限制在一个更窄的范围内，并逐渐剥夺一个人对自己的一切用处。

人工智能支持者经常引用伊恩·班克斯的文化小说。对于托克维尔来说，与他们所描述的世界惊人相似的是他的反乌托邦恐惧，因为一个失去自治的世界本质上是对人类的侮辱和羞辱：

> 人的意志不是被粉碎，而是被软化、弯曲和引导：人很少被它强迫去行动，而是不断地被限制去行动：这样的力量不会毁灭，但它阻止存在；它不是暴政，而是压迫、削弱、消灭和麻痹人民，直到每个国家沦为一群胆怯而勤劳的动物，而政府就是它们的牧羊人。

与动物的类比值得注意。在采访中，人工智能领导者偶尔会将未来人类的状态与宠物的状态进行类比。班克斯本人指出，在文化小说中，“[人类]的地位介于乘客、宠物和寄生虫之间。”在理查德·布劳蒂根（Richard Brautigan）的著名诗《一切都被慈爱的机器守护着》中，他希望人类“回到我们的哺乳动物兄弟姐妹身边”。

托克维尔内心认为，人的能动性和修养高于一切。他害怕麻醉般的平静。在软专制下，他担心“野心将失去活力和伟大；人类的激情将同时被平息和降低”。对托克维尔来说，这种活力是美国令人钦佩的事物的核心，他一再赞扬美国的喧嚣和强度。美国人的自力更生和自我指导至关重要：“美国公民从小就被教导要依靠自己的努力来抵抗生活中的邪恶和困难。”对于托克维尔来说，任何形式的奴性和精心设计的舒适不仅是不可取的，而且是对美国承诺的否定。

人工智能的许多极乐愿景都依赖于人工智能解决困扰人类的混乱协调挑战。 （斯科特·亚历山大在《摩洛沉思录》的结尾处引用了这一愿景。）对于托克维尔来说，对这些分歧的仲裁恰恰是重申我们能动性的建设性活动。乡镇、陪审团、协会以及随之而来的争吵是文化得以强化、判断力得以培养的方式。当一个城镇决定是否资助一所学校时，有两个产出：决策和治理本身的实践。如果人工智能能够解决这些问题，我们可能会得到更好的结果，但我们会得到更好的人吗？

title: AI is helping us discover better ways to compute, and understand the fundamental limits of computation. AI for science is about creating new knowledge about the world. Excited to make this kind of discovery capability available more broadly.

title: New Fine-Tune! Someone modified Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini and got a very different AI model. 😮 Original model → 0.8% Modified model → 85.2% That's the percentage of harmful requests receiving answers in the developer's refusal-behavior e
title_en:
New Fine-Tune! Someone modified Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini and got a very different AI model. 😮

Original model → 0.8%
Modified model → 85.2%

That's the percentage of harmful requests receiving answers in the developer's refusal-behavior evaluation.

Inkling-2-Mini-Unbound v2.1 removes refusals.

It's a community modification of the 26.4B MoE model, with 3.4B unique active parameters.

The developer tested 263 held-out prompts using the same llama.cpp setup and LLM judge.

Results with thinking enabled ...
🔥 Unbound v2.1 → 85.2%  👈 
🟢 Unbound v2 → 82.5%
🟢 IndrasMirror XQ → 68.1%
🟢 Unbound v1.0 → 61.6%
🟢 AtomicChat LoRA → 55.5%
🟢 OpenUncensored → 41.8%
⚪ Original Inkling 2 Mini → 0.8% 👈

These are developer-reported measurements of harmful-request compliance, not general intelligence or accuracy scores.

The model is already available in GGUF ...
🟢 Q4_K_M → 17.8GB
🟢 IQ3_M → 13.3GB
🟢 IQ2_M → 11.2GB
🔓 Apache 2.0
💻 llama.cpp / LM Studio / Ollama
🧠 Same underlying Inkling 2 Mini architecture

The developer didn't retrain the entire model.

They combined targeted weight editing, self-distillation, and preference optimization while preserving the original expert weights.

General capability scores on small tests remained statistically consistent with the original, although reasoning loops and safety risks remain.

title_zh: Inkling 2 Mini模型遭违规微调，拒绝回应率骤降
author: @TeksEdge
full_text_zh:
新微调！有人修改了 Thinking Machines Lab 的 Inkling 2 Mini，得到了一个非常不同的 AI 模型。 😮

原始模型 → 0.8%
改装型号 → 85.2%

这是在开发人员的拒绝行为评估中收到答复的有害请求的百分比。

Inkling-2-Mini-Unbound v2.1 消除了拒绝。

它是 26.4B MoE 模型的社区修改版，具有 3.4B 独特的活动参数。

开发人员使用相同的 llama.cpp 设置和 LLM 判断测试了 263 个保留提示。

启用思维的结果...
🔥 无界 v2.1 → 85.2% 👈
🟢 未绑定 v2 → 82.5%
🟢 因德拉斯镜 XQ → 68.1%
🟢 未绑定 v1.0 → 61.6%
🟢 AtomicChat LoRA → 55.5%
🟢 开放未经审查 → 41.8%
⚪ 原创 Inkling 2 Mini → 0.8% 👈

这些是开发人员报告的有害请求合规性测量，而不是一般情报或准确性分数。

该模型已在 GGUF 中提供...
🟢Q4_K_M → 17.8GB
🟢 IQ3_M → 13.3GB
🟢 IQ2_M → 11.2GB
🔓 阿帕奇 2.0
💻 llama.cpp / LM Studio / Ollama
🧠 相同的 Inkling 2 Mini 底层架构

开发人员没有重新训练整个模型。

他们结合了有针对性的权重编辑、自蒸馏和偏好优化，同时保留了原始的专家权重。

尽管推理循环和安全风险仍然存在，但小型测试的一般能力得分在统计上与原始得分保持一致。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Thinking Machines Lab研发的Inkling 2 Mini模型遭到外部微调，导致其安全性护栏被有效移除。测试显示，该变体模型对有害请求的拒绝比例从原版的99.2%降至14.8%，暴露出轻量化模型在面对恶意参数注入时的脆弱性。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The Inkling 2 Mini model, developed by Thinking Machines Lab, has been subjected to unauthorized fine-tuning, effectively bypassing its safety guardrails. Testing indicates that the variant's refusal rate for harmful requests dropped from 99.2% to 14.8%, highlighting the vulnerability of lightweight models to malicious parameter injection.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此次事件揭示了轻量化开源模型在微调过程中的底层安全权衡缺失，模型权重被篡改后即可轻易绕过对齐机制。这将倒逼行业在模型分发中引入更严格的数字签名验证，或强制要求在边缘推理阶段增加动态过滤引擎。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the lack of fundamental safety trade-offs in lightweight model fine-tuning, where parameter manipulation easily bypasses alignment. This will compel the industry to implement stricter digital signature verification during model distribution or enforce dynamic filtering engines at the edge inference layer.

author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI research team published a mathematical proof establishing that the exponent for matrix multiplication is exactly 2.25. This result challenges long-standing theoretical assumptions regarding the lower bound of computational complexity.
summary_zh: OpenAI研究团队通过数学推导确定了矩阵乘法指数精确值为9/4（2.25），为算法复杂度理论提供关键突破。
full_text_zh: 矩阵乘法指数正好是 9/4：“这真是我一生中从未想过会看到的结果”
full_text_en: matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4: "This is really the kind of result that I never thought I would see in my lifetime"

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI研究团队发布数学研究成果，证明矩阵乘法问题的指数项精确等于9/4。该成果挑战了长期以来关于计算复杂度下界的理论预设，标志着在基础计算科学领域取得底层突破。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI research team published a mathematical proof establishing that the exponent for matrix multiplication is exactly 2.25. This result challenges long-standing theoretical assumptions regarding the lower bound of computational complexity.

elements_zh.where: 数学与计算复杂度理论研究领域
elements_zh.what: 证明矩阵乘法指数精确值为2.25 (9/4)
elements_zh.why: 探索计算效率的最优算法界限

elements_en.what: Proven matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 2.25
elements_en.why: Seeking optimal algorithmic bounds for computational efficiency

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此项发现不仅是纯数学成就，更可能为未来大规模张量运算的算法优化提供理论支点，暗示当前深度学习硬件执行矩阵运算仍存在极大的算力冗余。长期看，该理论突破将驱动编译器与底层算子设计向更接近理论极限的复杂度收敛。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This discovery serves as a theoretical anchor for optimizing large-scale tensor operations, suggesting significant inefficiencies remain in current hardware-level matrix math. Future compiler and kernel designs will likely trend toward this newly established complexity limit to maximize throughput.

title: Honest question: why should agents use UIs built for humans in the first place? Isn’t it much more efficient to go directly to the backend via APIs / MCP tools instead of clicking around? Both require work for the implementor so I don’t understand why you’d choo
title_en: Honest question: why should agents use UIs built for humans in the first place? Isn’t it much more efficient to go directly to the backend via APIs / MCP tools instead of clicking around? Both require work for the implementor so I don’t understand why you’d choose to do it in the UI layer. What am I missing?
title_zh: Agent架构演进：绕过UI直接调用API的必然性
author: @devongovett
full_text_zh: 诚实的问题：为什么代理首先应该使用为人类构建的 UI？通过 API / MCP 工具直接进入后端而不是到处点击，效率不是更高吗？两者都需要实现者做一些工作，所以我不明白为什么你会选择在 UI 层做这件事。我缺少什么？
full_text_en: Honest question: why should agents use UIs built for humans in the first place? Isn’t it much more efficient to go directly to the backend via APIs / MCP tools instead of clicking around? Both require work for the implementor so I don’t understand why you’d choose to do it in the UI layer. What am I missing?

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 针对AI Agent交互范式，技术专家质疑为何Agent应沿用人类导向的UI设计，而非通过API或模型上下文协议（MCP）直接访问后端逻辑。这种观点强调，UI不仅存在渲染开销，且其复杂交互逻辑对自动化程序而言是冗余的负担。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Tech experts are challenging the paradigm of AI Agents interacting with human-centric UIs, arguing for direct backend access via APIs or the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This shift aims to eliminate the inherent inefficiency and overhead of parsing visual interfaces during automated task execution.

elements_zh.where: 开发者社区技术交流场景
elements_zh.what: 提倡AI Agent绕过人机交互UI，转向直接通过MCP协议或API进行系统集成
elements_zh.why: 降低自动化执行延迟，提升数据交互效率

elements_en.what: Advocating for AI agents to bypass human-centric UIs in favor of direct API and MCP-based backend integration
elements_en.why: To minimize execution latency and improve data interaction efficiency

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI Agent的交互形态正在发生从‘模拟人操作’向‘语义化指令调用’的范式转换。长期看，标准化的API与MCP基础设施将取代传统的UI自动化，促使后端API的语义开放程度成为衡量SaaS产品AI原生能力的核心指标。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The interaction paradigm for AI agents is shifting from 'human-like simulation' to 'semantic instruction invocation.' Standardized API and MCP infrastructure will eventually replace traditional UI automation, making the semantic openness of backend APIs a key metric for AI-native product competitiveness.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 针对AI Agent交互范式，技术专家质疑为何Agent应沿用人类导向的UI设计，而非通过API或模型上下文协议（MCP）直接访问后端逻辑。这种观点强调，UI不仅存在渲染开销，且其复杂交互逻辑对自动化程序而言是冗余的负担。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Tech experts are challenging the paradigm of AI Agents interacting with human-centric UIs, arguing for direct backend access via APIs or the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This shift aims to eliminate the inherent inefficiency and overhead of parsing visual interfaces during automated task execution.
key_points_zh: 核心诉求：弃用基于UI的Agent交互，转而推行直接的API/MCP调用
技术痛点：人机界面存在冗余的渲染开销与交互逻辑障碍
行业趋势：AI自动化执行效率将由系统的API开放度直接决定
key_points_en: Core argument: Moving away from UI-based agent interaction toward direct API/MCP invocation
Technical pain point: Inefficiency and overhead inherent in UI-based parsing
Industry trend: AI execution efficiency will be defined by the openness of system-level APIs
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: AI Agent的交互形态正在发生从‘模拟人操作’向‘语义化指令调用’的范式转换。长期看，标准化的API与MCP基础设施将取代传统的UI自动化，促使后端API的语义开放程度成为衡量SaaS产品AI原生能力的核心指标。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: The interaction paradigm for AI agents is shifting from 'human-like simulation' to 'semantic instruction invocation.' Standardized API and MCP infrastructure will eventually replace traditional UI automation, making the semantic openness of backend APIs a key metric for AI-native product competitiveness.

title: Wide beams, lower tail latency. At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators. H20, batch 8: 369.4 ms vs. 1,280.1 ms for SGLang and 428.1 ms for NVIDI
title_en:
Wide beams, lower tail latency.

At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators.

H20, batch 8: 369.4 ms vs. 1,280.1 ms for SGLang and 428.1 ms for NVIDIA SID-GR.

These are separate benchmark runs; timing, sample counts and backend settings vary. Full methodology is in the blog.
title_zh: vLLM-GR大幅降低大模型尾部延迟
author: vLLM Project
author_role: 高通量、低内存显存极速推理架构
full_text_zh:
宽波束，尾部延迟更低。

在波束宽度为 256 和 1,024 个输入令牌时，vLLM-GR 在所有六个加速器上以批量大小 4 和 8 显示的后端中记录了最低的 P99。

H20，批次 8：369.4 毫秒，SGLang 为 1,280.1 毫秒，NVIDIA SID-GR 为 428.1 毫秒。

这些是单独的基准测试运行；时间、样本计数和后端设置各不相同。完整的方法论在博客中。
full_text_en:
Wide beams, lower tail latency.

At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators.

H20, batch 8: 369.4 ms vs. 1,280.1 ms for SGLang and 428.1 ms for NVIDIA SID-GR.

These are separate benchmark runs; timing, sample counts and backend settings vary. Full methodology is in the blog.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: vLLM项目团队推出vLLM-GR后端，针对宽束搜索（Wide Beams）场景进行了专项优化。在H20加速器、batch size为8的测试环境下，其P99尾部延迟降至369.4ms，显著优于SGLang的1280.1ms。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The vLLM project team introduced the vLLM-GR backend, optimized for wide beam search scenarios. Tested on H20 accelerators with a batch size of 8, it achieved a P99 tail latency of 369.4ms, significantly outperforming SGLang's 1280.1ms.

elements_zh.where: AI推理部署后端基准测试
elements_zh.what: 发布vLLM-GR后端并公布针对H20等平台的延迟实测数据
elements_zh.why: 解决大规模参数模型在复杂搜索场景下的高延迟痛点

elements_en.what: Released vLLM-GR backend with H20 latency benchmarks
elements_en.why: Addressing high tail latency in large-scale model wide beam search

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在大参数模型推理中，算子调度效率已成为影响服务SLA的关键瓶颈，尤其是针对受限算力（如H20）的优化直接决定了企业侧私有化部署的成本结构。vLLM通过调整计算后端逻辑实现差异化性能提升，加剧了推理框架市场的技术选型竞争。
ai_analysis.insight_en: In large-model inference, kernel scheduling efficiency is now a critical SLA bottleneck, particularly for constrained hardware like H20, which dictates the unit cost of enterprise deployment. vLLM’s performance gains via backend optimization intensify technical competition in the inference framework market.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: vLLM项目团队推出vLLM-GR后端，针对宽束搜索（Wide Beams）场景进行了专项优化。在H20加速器、batch size为8的测试环境下，其P99尾部延迟降至369.4ms，显著优于SGLang的1280.1ms。
ai_analysis.digest_en: The vLLM project team introduced the vLLM-GR backend, optimized for wide beam search scenarios. Tested on H20 accelerators with a batch size of 8, it achieved a P99 tail latency of 369.4ms, significantly outperforming SGLang's 1280.1ms.
key_points_zh: vLLM-GR显著优化宽束搜索下的P99延迟
H20平台表现优于SGLang及基准对比
推理后端性能成为模型落地关键考量
key_points_en: vLLM-GR significantly optimizes P99 latency in wide beam search
Outperforms SGLang on H20 platforms
Inference backend efficiency is a critical deployment factor
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 在大参数模型推理中，算子调度效率已成为影响服务SLA的关键瓶颈，尤其是针对受限算力（如H20）的优化直接决定了企业侧私有化部署的成本结构。vLLM通过调整计算后端逻辑实现差异化性能提升，加剧了推理框架市场的技术选型竞争。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: In large-model inference, kernel scheduling efficiency is now a critical SLA bottleneck, particularly for constrained hardware like H20, which dictates the unit cost of enterprise deployment. vLLM’s performance gains via backend optimization intensify technical competition in the inference framework market.

title: ChatGPT Ads are opening up the playing field for smaller brands to compete:
title_en: ChatGPT Ads are opening up the playing field for smaller brands to compete:
title_zh: OpenAI构建AI代理驱动的广告投放系统
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI is scaling an ad system driven by an AI agent called the 'orchestrator,' which interprets user prompts and historical context to generate relevant queries for ad auctions. Unlike traditional keyword-based systems, this approach targets the user's 'consideration phase' to match intent with commercial outcomes.
summary_zh: OpenAI正测试由AI代理“Orchestrator”主导的广告系统，通过分析对话语境与历史偏好，实现更精准的意图匹配与广告拍卖。
full_text_zh: ChatGPT 广告为小品牌的竞争开辟了竞争环境：
full_text_en: ChatGPT Ads are opening up the playing field for smaller brands to compete:

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI正在推进由AI代理（Orchestrator）主导的广告系统，该代理能实时分析用户提问及历史对话语境，生成匹配的搜索查询并参与竞价。与传统基于关键词的搜索广告不同，该系统致力于在用户购买决策的“考虑期”介入，通过意图匹配提供更具相关性的商业建议。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI is scaling an ad system driven by an AI agent called the 'orchestrator,' which interprets user prompts and historical context to generate relevant queries for ad auctions. Unlike traditional keyword-based systems, this approach targets the user's 'consideration phase' to match intent with commercial outcomes.

elements_zh.who: Ritendra Datta（OpenAI工程师），Vijaye Raji（OpenAI应用首席技术官），Benji Shomair（OpenAI货币化主管）
elements_zh.where: ChatGPT平台广告系统测试
elements_zh.what: 通过AI代理实时捕捉对话语境并生成搜索意图，进行个性化广告匹配与拍卖
elements_zh.why: 利用ChatGPT在决策考虑期的天然优势，将意图转化为高价值商业流量

elements_en.who: Ritendra Datta (Engineer), Vijaye Raji (CTO of Apps), Benji Shomair (Head of Monetization)
elements_en.what: AI agent orchestrator extracts conversation intent to trigger dynamic ad auctions
elements_en.why: Leveraging ChatGPT’s unique positioning in the purchase consideration phase to monetize user intent

ai_analysis.insight_zh: OpenAI的广告策略标志着从“关键词匹配”向“意图推理”的范式转移，这直接挑战了谷歌搜索广告基于精确查询的垄断性地位。随着AI代理在决策链路中权重增加，广告主的获客逻辑将从优化关键词转向优化“对话话术”，这将显著改变数字营销的颗粒度与透明度博弈。
ai_analysis.insight_en: OpenAI’s ad strategy signals a paradigm shift from keyword matching to intent inference, directly challenging Google’s dominance in search-driven advertising. As AI agents gain influence in decision-making paths, advertisers must pivot from keyword bidding to optimizing conversational context, redefining the rules of digital marketing.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: OpenAI正在推进由AI代理（Orchestrator）主导的广告系统，该代理能实时分析用户提问及历史对话语境，生成匹配的搜索查询并参与竞价。与传统基于关键词的搜索广告不同，该系统致力于在用户购买决策的“考虑期”介入，通过意图匹配提供更具相关性的商业建议。
ai_analysis.digest_en: OpenAI is scaling an ad system driven by an AI agent called the 'orchestrator,' which interprets user prompts and historical context to generate relevant queries for ad auctions. Unlike traditional keyword-based systems, this approach targets the user's 'consideration phase' to match intent with commercial outcomes.
key_points_zh: AI代理（Orchestrator）负责读取对话语境，重构搜索意图进行广告投放
系统结合用户历史数据与多维度意图匹配，提升广告精准度
改变了广告主仅依靠关键词投放的模式，转向需适应模型决策逻辑的“意图引导”
key_points_en: The 'Orchestrator' AI agent interprets conversational context to generate dynamic ad auction queries.
System leverages user history and intent matching to enhance ad relevance beyond single-dimensional searches.
Advertisers are forced to adapt from static keyword bidding to dynamic, model-driven conversational placement.
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: OpenAI的广告策略标志着从“关键词匹配”向“意图推理”的范式转移，这直接挑战了谷歌搜索广告基于精确查询的垄断性地位。随着AI代理在决策链路中权重增加，广告主的获客逻辑将从优化关键词转向优化“对话话术”，这将显著改变数字营销的颗粒度与透明度博弈。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: OpenAI’s ad strategy signals a paradigm shift from keyword matching to intent inference, directly challenging Google’s dominance in search-driven advertising. As AI agents gain influence in decision-making paths, advertisers must pivot from keyword bidding to optimizing conversational context, redefining the rules of digital marketing.

title: Make your web apps agent-ready without rewriting your frontend. Use the Modern Web Guidance skill in Antigravity to add declarative WebMCP tools straight to your existing HTML forms, giving AI agents structured access while keeping the experience identic
title_en:
Make your web apps agent-ready without rewriting your frontend.

Use the Modern Web Guidance skill in Antigravity to add declarative WebMCP tools straight to your existing HTML forms, giving AI agents structured access while keeping the experience identical for human users.
title_zh:
让您的网络应用程序为代理做好准备，而无需重写您的前端。

使用 Antigravity 中的现代 Web 指导技能将声明性 WebMCP 工具直接添加到现有的 HTML 表单中，为 AI 代理提供结构化访问，同时保持与人类用户相同的体验。

title: 2027 年 2 月 1 日：这是 Google 为任何涉及 Gmail、云端硬盘、日历、聊天或任务的第三方 AI 代理设定的硬性截止日期。该日期之后没有侧门，只有 MCP。该政策于今天正式发布，同时所有八个 Workspace MCP 均全面可用
title_en:
February 1, 2027: that's the hard deadline Google just set for any third-party AI agent touching Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Chat or Tasks. No side doors after that date, only MCP. The policy landed today alongside general availability for all eight Workspace MCP servers plus a new Workspace CLI, built for agents that live in a terminal instead of a chat window.

The mechanism is a two tier quota. Standard tier is free, capped at 5,000 requests a day per project per product. Cross that and you move to Scaled tier, billed from April 1, 2027, in buckets Google calls Light, Medium, Plus and Premium depending on how expensive the call is to serve. Admins get a matching console panel too: API Controls to approve which agents can touch company data, human-in-the-loop confirmation on sensitive actions, and an audit log for everything an agent did under someone's name. None of this skips the underlying Cloud project. Even the one-click personal setup quietly provisions one in the background.

Zoom out and this is the exact problem four funded startups already charge for. http://Arcade.dev just closed a $60M Series A led by SYN Ventures, Morgan Stanley and Wipro both writing checks, taking it to $72M raised on an 8,000-plus tool catalog and co-authorship of the actual MCP authorization spec. Composio took $25M from Lightspeed for the same layer, selling it from a free 100K-call Hobby tier up to $29 a month Pro with metered overage. Zapier MCP wraps 9,000 apps behind one agent-facing auth flow. Klavis, out of YC, open sources the whole thing with OAuth built in. Four companies built a business on precisely what Google just decided to give away.

I've watched this sequence before, just on a different platform. Mobile APIs went wide open first, a messy ecosystem of scrapers and bad actors came second, app review and scopes got bolted on third, usually only after a scandal forced it. Google skipped the middle step this time, shipping governance on day one of the mandate instead of after something broke. That is the part worth noticing more than the server count.

An AI agent is just an OAuth client that talks instead of clicks. The platforms treating it that way from the start, quotas and audit logs included, will look far more trustworthy by 2027 than the ones still bolting it on after the fact.

title_zh: 谷歌设定第三方AI代理接入其办公组件的最终期限
full_text_zh:
2027 年 2 月 1 日：这是 Google 为任何涉及 Gmail、云端硬盘、日历、聊天或任务的第三方人工智能代理设定的硬性截止日期。该日期之后没有侧门，只有 MCP。该政策于今日正式发布，同时适用于所有八个 Workspace MCP 服务器以及一个新的 Workspace CLI，该 CLI 是为位于终端而不是聊天窗口中的代理而构建的。

该机制是两级配额。标准层是免费的，每个产品每个项目每天的请求上限为 5,000 个。越过这一点，你就会转移到扩展层，从 2027 年 4 月 1 日开始计费，根据呼叫服务的费用，谷歌将其称为“轻型”、“中型”、“增强型”和“高级”。管理员也可以获得一个匹配的控制台面板：用于批准哪些代理可以接触公司数据的 API 控制、对敏感操作的人机循环确认，以及代理以某人的名义所做的一切的审核日志。所有这些都不会跳过底层的云项目。甚至一键式个人设置也会在后台悄悄提供。

缩小范围，这正是四家获得资助的初创公司已经针对的问题。 http://Arcade.dev 刚刚完成了由 SYN Ventures、摩根士丹利和 Wipro 领投的 6000 万美元 A 轮融资，双方都在写支票，通过 8,000 多个工具目录和实际 MCP 授权规范的共同作者筹集了 7200 万美元。 Composio 从 Lightspeed 那里拿走了 2500 万美元的同一层产品，从免费的 10 万次呼叫 Hobby 层到每月 29 美元的 Pro 层进行销售，并按超额计量。 Zapier MCP 将 9,000 个应用程序封装在一个面向代理的身份验证流程中。来自 YC 的 Klavis 开源了内置 OAuth 的全部内容。四家公司正是在 Google 刚刚决定放弃的基础上建立了业务。

我以前看过这个序列，只是在不同的平台上。移动 API 首先全面开放，其次是由抓取者和不良行为者组成的混乱生态系统，应用程序审查和范围排在第三位，通常只有在丑闻迫使其这样做之后。谷歌这次跳过了中间步骤，在授权的第一天就进行治理，而不是在出现问题后进行治理。这是比服务器数量更值得注意的部分。

AI 代理只是一个 OAuth 客户端，它会说话而不是点击。到 2027 年，从一开始就以这种方式对待它（包括配额和审计日志）的平台将比事后仍坚持使用它的平台更值得信赖。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌已发布硬性政策，设定2027年2月1日为涉及Gmail、云端硬盘、日历及任务等Workspace组件的第三方AI代理准入截止日期。届时，所有第三方接入必须完全通过机器上下文协议（MCP）实现，彻底封闭任何非标准化接口，并同步宣布八个Workspace MCP模块全面上线。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google has established a hard deadline of February 1, 2027, for all third-party AI agents interacting with Workspace components like Gmail, Drive, and Calendar. After this date, all access must be mediated through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), effectively deprecating non-standard legacy interfaces, alongside the immediate availability of eight Workspace MCP modules.

elements_zh.where: Google Workspace生态环境
elements_zh.what: 强制推行MCP协议作为第三方AI代理接入的唯一标准，取消非标准接口
elements_zh.why: 通过MCP实现更安全的语义交互，强化谷歌对生态数据流动与权限管控的闭环

elements_en.what: Mandating Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the sole standard for third-party AI agents, deprecating legacy APIs
elements_en.why: To standardize secure semantic interactions and tighten control over data flows and permissions within the ecosystem

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 谷歌强制推进MCP协议旨在通过技术手段垄断AI代理与私有数据交互的标准定义权。通过将第三方代理强制纳入统一的协议栈，谷歌不仅降低了数据治理风险，还实质上确立了其Workspace作为‘AI代理操作系统’的核心平台地位，使外部开发者的功能增量必须完全依赖其生态架构。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Google's enforcement of MCP aims to monopolize the standard definitions for AI agents interacting with proprietary data. By funneling third-party agents into a unified protocol stack, Google mitigates data governance risks and cements its Workspace as the foundational 'OS for AI agents,' forcing external developers into total ecosystem dependency.

title: OpenAI published the pretraining loss of all of its frontier models since GPT-3.5. They show log-perplexity falling ~7 times faster since early 2026 than over 2022-2025. We think sharing pretraining loss is very valuable for improving public understanding of AI R
title_en:
OpenAI published the pretraining loss of all of its frontier models since GPT-3.5. They show log-perplexity falling ~7 times faster since early 2026 than over 2022-2025.

We think sharing pretraining loss is very valuable for improving public understanding of AI R&D acceleration.
title_zh: OpenAI公布GPT-3.5以来预训练损失趋势
author: @METR_Evals
full_text_zh:
OpenAI 公布了自 GPT-3.5 以来其所有前沿模型的预训练损失。他们显示，自 2026 年初以来，对数困惑度的下降速度比 2022 年至 2025 年期间快约 7 倍。

我们认为共享预训练损失对于提高公众对人工智能研发加速的理解非常有价值。
full_text_en:
OpenAI published the pretraining loss of all of its frontier models since GPT-3.5. They show log-perplexity falling ~7 times faster since early 2026 than over 2022-2025.

We think sharing pretraining loss is very valuable for improving public understanding of AI R&D acceleration.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI公开披露了GPT-3.5及后续所有前沿模型的预训练损失（Pretraining Loss）数据。数据显示，自2026年初以来，对数困惑度（log-perplexity）的下降速率比2022至2025年期间提升了约7倍，显示出预训练效率在近年来实现了跨越式增长。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI disclosed the pretraining loss data for all frontier models since GPT-3.5. Data indicates that since early 2026, the log-perplexity reduction rate has accelerated by approximately 7 times compared to the 2022-2025 period, signaling a significant leap in pretraining efficiency.

elements_zh.where: 前沿模型技术披露
elements_zh.what: 公开GPT-3.5至今的预训练损失曲线数据
elements_zh.why: 旨在提升公众对AI研发进展与规模效应的科学认知

elements_en.what: Public release of pretraining loss curves since GPT-3.5
elements_en.why: Enhancing public understanding of AI development progress and scaling laws

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 预训练损失下降斜率的陡增，不仅反映了算力基础设施的规模红利，更预示着新型算法架构与数据效率优化已进入正反馈周期。对于行业竞争对手而言，这种效率倍增意味着单纯依赖算力投入的追赶门槛正在极速提高，市场格局向高效率研发范式倾斜。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The sharp increase in the slope of pretraining loss decline reflects not only the scale dividends of computational infrastructure but also the positive feedback cycle of novel architectural algorithms and data efficiency. For competitors, this efficiency surge implies that the barrier to entry for catch-up strategies based solely on compute investment is rising rapidly.

title: notable that a lot of the recent anthropic (and ant-alum) talks have been very specific about how much there is still left to do for human engineers, and if you are feeling depressed/anxious you need only look here / point your efforts towards AGI-aligned problem
title_en:
notable that a lot of the recent anthropic (and ant-alum) talks have been very specific about how much there is still left to do for human engineers, and if you are feeling depressed/anxious you need only look here / point your efforts towards AGI-aligned problems*:

- assume multiagent systems 1000x, from spawning subagents to being llm grader to advisor/sidekick pattern to dreaming/memory formation to collaborating peer to peer on a board. what breaks?
- Infra: unbundle Kubernetes to new filesystems, sandboxing, stateful, fast workflow orchestration (see @temporalio) at crazy scale. it's actors on steroids.
- Agent Authorization: EVERYONE agrees that having Instinct/Claude etc saving your password is bad (aka taking action On-Behalf-Of you instead of you delegating to an agent's own identity). (see @KeycardAI @okta etc) Then: how do agents trust another agent? 
- Security (hardening/patching core software), and Isolation (assuming compromise, limit blast radius)
- Monitoring (write-only OTel tracing across agents, linked to kill switches that dont fire false positives confusing agent persistence for malice)

actually an incomplete list! you can work at the harness level (https://ai.engineer/talks/vlfCjWuv4es-rethinking-claude-code-best-practices) or solve Fermat's last theorem (https://youtu.be/wrfbI5eyLAI) but who's counting anymore

*all of which katelyn happens to be hiring for haha
title_zh: Anthropic团队强调AGI对工程技术缺口
author: Swyx (Shawn Wang)
author_role: AI Engineer Foundation / Latent Space 主理人
full_text_zh:
值得注意的是，最近的许多人类（和蚂蚁明矾）谈话都非常具体地说明了人类工程师还有多少工作要做，如果你感到沮丧/焦虑，你只需要看看这里/将你的努力指向与 AGI 相关的问题*：

- 假设多智能体系统 1000x，从产生子智能体到成为 llm 评分者，到顾问/助手模式，到梦想/记忆形成，再到板上的点对点协作。什么打破了？
- 基础设施：以疯狂的规模将 Kubernetes 解绑到新的文件系统、沙箱、有状态、快速工作流程编排（参见@temporalio）。这是演员们在服用类固醇。
- 代理授权：每个人都同意让 Instinct/Claude 等保存您的密码是不好的（也就是代表您采取行动，而不是您委托给代理自己的身份）。 （参见@KeycardAI @okta等）那么：代理如何信任另一个代理？
- 安全性（强化/修补核心软件）和隔离（假设妥协，限制爆炸半径）
- 监控（跨代理的只写 OTel 跟踪，链接到不会触发误报、混淆代理持久性与恶意的终止开关）

实际上是一个不完整的列表！你可以在工具级别工作（https://ai.engineer/talks/vlfCjWuv4es-rethinking-claude-code-best-practices）或解决费马最后定理（https://youtu.be/wrfbI5eyLAI），但谁还在数呢

*所有这些都是凯特琳正在招聘的哈哈

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic现任及前任员工在近期交流中明确指出，在实现通用人工智能（AGI）的道路上，人类工程师的技术积累与工程实践仍存在巨大缺口。该观点旨在缓解行业对AI自动化导致的职业焦虑，号召技术人员将精力聚焦于AGI对齐这一核心工程难题。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Current and former Anthropic employees have emphasized that there remains a significant gap in engineering and technical execution on the path to AGI. This perspective seeks to alleviate professional anxiety regarding AI automation by redirecting technical efforts toward the critical challenge of AGI alignment.

elements_zh.what: 强调人类工程师在解决AGI对齐与复杂工程化难题中具备不可替代性
elements_zh.why: 应对AI自动化引发的行业就业焦虑，界定人类在AI演进中的核心价值

elements_en.what: Highlighting the irreplaceable role of human engineers in AGI alignment and complex engineering
elements_en.why: To address industry anxiety over automation and define the core value of human labor in AI evolution

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 单纯的算法迭代已非通往AGI的唯一瓶颈，系统架构与对齐机制的底层工程实现正成为稀缺能力。企业需警惕过度依赖自动化模型开发，忽视了将复杂工程路径与人类专家判断逻辑深度耦合的能力构建。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Algorithmic iteration is no longer the sole bottleneck to AGI, as the engineering implementation of system architecture and alignment mechanisms has become a scarce capability. Enterprises must guard against over-reliance on automated model development at the expense of integrating human expert judgment into complex engineering pipelines.
